questions.question: Who is the author of the story 'The Beggar'?
questions.explanation: The story 'The Beggar' is written by the famous Russian writer Anton Chekhov.

questions.question: What is the name of the advocate in the story?
questions.explanation: The advocate who confronts the beggar is named Sergei.

questions.question: At the beginning of the story, what does the beggar claim was his profession for eight years?
questions.explanation: The beggar tells Sergei, 'For eight years I was a village school teacher'.

questions.question: Why did the beggar claim he lost his job as a teacher?
questions.explanation: He claimed he lost his place through 'intrigues'.

questions.question: What colour was the beggar's ragged overcoat?
questions.explanation: The text describes his overcoat as 'ragged, fawn-coloured'.

questions.question: In which province did the beggar claim to have an offer of a position?
questions.explanation: He claimed to have an offer in the province of Kaluga.

questions.question: What specific detail about the beggar's footwear helped Sergei remember him?

options.C: One overshoe was high and the other low.

questions.explanation: Sergei's eyes fell on the overshoes, 'one of which was high and the other low'.

questions.question: Where did Sergei claim to have met the beggar two days prior?
questions.explanation: Sergei says, 'it seems to me I met you the day before yesterday in Sadovya Street'.

questions.question: When Sergei first met him in Sadovya Street, what did the beggar pretend to be?
questions.explanation: In their previous meeting, the beggar told Sergei he was a student who had been expelled.

questions.question: What was the beggar's actual previous job before becoming a beggar?

options.B: He sang in a Russian choir.

questions.explanation: The beggar eventually confesses, 'Formerly I sang in a Russian choir'.

questions.question: Why was the beggar sent away from the Russian choir?
questions.explanation: He admits he was 'sent away for drunkenness'.

questions.question: What does 'swindling' mean according to the glossary?
questions.explanation: The glossary defines 'swindling' as cheating a person of money.

questions.question: What work did Sergei first offer the beggar?
questions.explanation: Sergei asks, 'How would you like to chop wood for me?'.

questions.question: Who was Olga in the story?
questions.explanation: Sergei calls his cook, Olga, to take the beggar to the woodshed.

questions.question: The beggar is described as a 'scarecrow'. What does this imply?

options.B: He looked thin, ragged, and pathetic.

questions.explanation: The term 'scarecrow of a beggar' refers to his ragged and unhealthy physical appearance.

questions.question: What had 'undermined' the beggar's strength, making him unhealthy?
questions.explanation: The text states his strength had been 'undermined by vodka'.

questions.question: What does the word 'perplexities' mean in the context of the beggar's reaction?
questions.explanation: He shrugged his shoulders 'as if in perplexity' (confusion) when asked to work.

questions.question: How did Olga treat the beggar when they first went to the woodshed?

options.B: She glared wrathfully and shoved him.

questions.explanation: Olga 'glared wrathfully... shoved him aside with her elbow... and angrily banged the door'.

questions.question: How much was the beggar paid the first time he finished chopping wood?
questions.explanation: Sergei tells Olga, 'Give him half a rouble'.

questions.question: On what day of the month did the beggar usually appear to work?

options.B: The first day of each month
options.D: The last day of the month

questions.explanation: Sergei suggested he could 'come back and cut wood on the first day of each month'.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a task the beggar did at Sergei's yard?
questions.explanation: The tasks mentioned are shovelling snow, ordering the shed, and beating rugs. Cooking was Olga's job.

questions.question: What is a 'rouble'?

options.B: The basic unit of Russian currency

questions.explanation: Roubles and copecks are the Russian currency units mentioned throughout the story.

questions.question: What is the name of the beggar revealed to be?
questions.explanation: When Sergei asks for his name, he replies, 'Lushkoff'.

questions.question: Why did Sergei send Lushkoff to his friend with a letter?

options.B: To give him some copying to do

questions.explanation: Sergei offers him 'cleaner employment' involving 'copying'.

questions.question: How many years passed before Sergei saw Lushkoff again after the copying job?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'Two years went by'.

questions.question: Where did Sergei meet Lushkoff after two years?

options.B: At the ticket window of a theatre

questions.explanation: Sergei was 'standing at the ticket window of a theatre' when he noticed Lushkoff.

questions.question: What was Lushkoff wearing when he met Sergei at the theatre?

options.B: A coat with a curly fur collar and a sealskin cap

questions.explanation: Lushkoff was now dressed well, with a 'coat collar of curly fur and a worn sealskin cap'.

questions.question: What was Lushkoff's profession when he met Sergei at the theatre?
questions.explanation: Lushkoff tells Sergei, 'I am a notary now'.

questions.question: How much was Lushkoff being paid a month as a notary?
questions.explanation: He says he is 'paid thirty-five roubles a month'.

questions.question: Sergei calls Lushkoff his '________' because he helped him find the right path.
questions.explanation: Sergei says, 'You see, you are my godson, in a sense'.

questions.question: According to Lushkoff, who actually saved him and set him right?
questions.explanation: Lushkoff explicitly states, 'it was your cook, Olga, who saved me'.

questions.question: How did Olga help Lushkoff in the woodshed?

options.B: She chopped all the wood for him.
options.C: She taught him how to sing.
options.D: She bought him a new coat.

questions.explanation: Lushkoff reveals, 'she used to chop the wood for me... I did not chop one single stick of wood for you'.

questions.question: What made Lushkoff stop drinking?
questions.explanation: He says, 'owing to her words and noble deeds, a change took place in my heart; she set me right'.

questions.question: What does the word 'mendicant' mean?
questions.explanation: The glossary identifies 'mendicant' as a synonym for beggar.

questions.question: What is a 'copeck'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: copeck - Russian coin equal to 1/100 of a rouble.

questions.question: What does 'billet' refer to in the story?
questions.explanation: Glossary: billet - a thick piece of wood.

questions.question: What is a 'waif'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: waif - a homeless person.

questions.question: Lushkoff calls Olga a 'good and ________ woman'.
questions.explanation: He says, 'God bless that good and noble woman!'.

questions.question: When Lushkoff was helping Sergei move, how did he behave?

options.B: He was sober, gloomy, and silent.

questions.explanation: During the move, 'the waif was sober, gloomy, and silent. He hardly touched the furniture'.

questions.question: Why did Sergei get angry and threaten the beggar with the police?

options.A: Because the beggar stole his watch.
options.B: Because the beggar was being dishonest and lying about his past.
options.C: Because the beggar refused to work.
options.D: Because the beggar was singing too loudly.

questions.explanation: Sergei cried 'This is swindling!' after catching the beggar in a lie.

questions.question: What does the word 'anguish' mean in the context of Lushkoff being accused of lying?
questions.explanation: Glossary: anguish - severe mental suffering.

questions.question: Lushkoff says Olga used to call him a '________' (meaning a habitual drunkard).
questions.explanation: Glossary: sot - a habitual drunkard. He quotes her saying, 'Oh, you sot, you!'.

questions.question: Sergei felt 'sorry and ashamed' for setting the beggar to '________ labour'.
questions.explanation: He felt bad for making a sick, drunken man do 'menial labour' in the cold.

questions.question: According to the story, 'a man of truth must also be a man of ________'.
questions.explanation: Sergei notes that 'a man of truth must also be a man of care'.

questions.question: What does 'roasting' mean in the context of Sergei scolding Lushkoff?
questions.explanation: Glossary: roasting - (here) scolding. Lushkoff asks, 'Do you remember what a roasting I gave you?'.

questions.question: Lushkoff paid for his theatre seat in ________ coins.
questions.explanation: He asked for a seat in the gallery and 'paid for it in copper coins'.

questions.question: Which specific street is mentioned where Sergei previously met the beggar?
questions.explanation: The street was 'Sadovya Street'.

questions.question: Lushkoff says, 'By flying to your ________ I dragged myself out of a pit.'
questions.explanation: Lushkoff attributes his recovery to Sergei's protection.

questions.question: What does 'taken aback' mean in the sentence 'mumbled the beggar, taken aback'?
questions.explanation: The context implies the beggar was surprised to be caught in a lie.

questions.question: Olga told Lushkoff that he would 'burn in ________'.
questions.explanation: Olga scolded him saying, 'You drunkard! You will burn in hell'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'fiction' in the story?
questions.explanation: Glossary: fiction - imaginary story.

questions.question: Lushkoff says, 'I shall be ________ to you to my dying day'.
questions.explanation: He expresses deep gratitude to Sergei.

questions.question: Lushkoff's change of heart was triggered by Olga's '________ deeds'.
questions.explanation: He credits her 'noble deeds' for the change in his heart.

questions.question: What is the tone of Olga's scolding according to Lushkoff?
questions.explanation: Lushkoff notes how many tears she shed for his sake while scolding him.

questions.question: What 'instrument' for chopping wood did Olga fling at Lushkoff's feet?
questions.explanation: Olga 'flung down an axe at his feet'.

questions.question: What word means 'wearing old torn clothes'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: ragged - wearing old torn clothes.

questions.question: Sergei was an 'advocate'. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: An advocate is another word for a lawyer.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'intrigue'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: intrigue - a secret plot / plan.

questions.question: What is 'vodka' described as in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: vodka - a colourless strong alcoholic drink.

questions.question: Lushkoff's face at the theater was 'near the ________' of Sergei when he mumbled goodbye.
questions.explanation: Wait, the source says 'With his face near the tiger’s' in a different story. For 'The Beggar', Lushkoff 'bowed and departed' after the bell.

questions.question: In the story 'The Beggar', Sergei is ________ when he finds out Lushkoff is a notary.
questions.explanation: Sergei says, 'I am delighted for your sake. I am very very glad, Lushkoff'.

questions.question: How did Lushkoff's eyes look when he was a beggar?
questions.explanation: The text describes his 'dull, drunken eyes'.

questions.question: What 'red spot' was visible on the beggar's face?
questions.explanation: The text mentions 'the red spot on either cheek'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'suppliant'?

options.A: A person making a humble request
options.B: A person who is very rich

questions.explanation: Glossary: suppliant - a person making humble request.

questions.question: Lushkoff claimed he was 'obliged to by ________' to ask for help.
questions.explanation: He says, 'I am obliged to by circumstances'.

questions.question: Sergei's face 'flushed' with what emotion when he caught Lushkoff lying?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'Sergei flushed and turned... with an expression of disgust'.

questions.question: What does 'flush' mean in the glossary?
questions.explanation: Glossary: flush - become red.

questions.question: Lushkoff says, 'No one will give me anything when I tell the ________'.
questions.explanation: Lushkoff admits he lies because no one helps him when he is honest about his drinking.

questions.question: Sergei felt Lushkoff had been '________ by his own words'.
questions.explanation: The beggar consented to work because he had been 'trapped by his own words' after being caught in a lie.

questions.question: What does 'menial' labour refer to?
questions.explanation: Sergei refers to the physical chores as 'menial labour'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'feebly' in 'tapped it feebly with the axe'?
questions.explanation: Lushkoff was physically weak and tapped the wood without much force.

questions.question: How much could Lushkoff earn for other tasks like beating rugs?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'Every time he received from twenty to forty copecks'.

questions.question: What piece of clothing was once sent out to Lushkoff at Sergei's yard?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'once, even a pair of old trousers was sent out to him'.

questions.question: Lushkoff 'sinks into the ground' metaphorically because of what?
questions.explanation: Sergei says, 'I nearly had you sinking into the ground... that day' during the scolding.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'indebted'?
questions.explanation: Lushkoff says he will be 'indebted' to Sergei for the rest of his life.

questions.question: Olga would sit down and '________' while looking at Lushkoff's face.
questions.explanation: Lushkoff recalls how Olga would 'look into my face and weep'.

questions.question: Lushkoff says, 'she set me ________ and I shall never forget it'.
questions.explanation: He credits Olga for setting him on the right path.

questions.question: In the theatre, Lushkoff timidly asked for a seat in the ________.
questions.explanation: He 'timidly asked the ticket seller for a seat in the gallery'.

questions.question: What 'signal' indicated it was time for Lushkoff to enter the theatre?
questions.explanation: He says, 'However, it is time to go now; there goes the bell'.

questions.question: What is the central theme of 'The Beggar'?

options.B: The power of kindness and noble deeds in transforming a life
options.C: The history of the Russian choir
options.D: The benefits of becoming a notary

questions.explanation: The story shows how Olga's selfless sacrifice and pity actually changed Lushkoff's heart.
